name: mmfit
paper_title: MM-Fit: Multimodal Deep Learning for Automatic Exercise Logging across Sensing Devices
authors: David Stromback, Sangxia Huang, Valentin Radu
venue: Proceedings of the ACM on Interactive, Mobile, Wearable and Ubiquitous Technologies (IMWUT) 4(4):168
license: Dataset: see mmfit.github.io. Paper PDF from the corresponding author's institutional page.
notes: 21 full workouts of 10 exercises, each captured SIMULTANEOUSLY on two smartwatches (both wrists), a smartphone in the right trouser pocket and an earbud, plus RGB-D video and 2D/3D pose (not converted). VERIFIED AT CONVERT TIME: every one of the 21 workouts has all four devices with both acc and gyr; accelerometer is m/s^2 with gravity (median |acc| 9.82-10.07 per device) and gyroscope is rad/s (p99.9 4-8). MEASURED, AND THE REASON RESAMPLING IS NOT OPTIONAL: the four devices log at genuinely different and non-uniform mean rates — 103 Hz and 104 Hz for the watches, 212 Hz for the phone, 85 Hz for the earbud — on a shared wall clock whose worst start-time skew across all workouts is 0.06 s. The converter resamples all four onto one 100 Hz grid, which is what makes the placements simultaneous sample-for-sample. Labels are start_frame,end_frame,reps,exercise against the same frame counter as column 0 of every .npy, so label frames are mapped to wall clock through that column. CAVEAT: MM-Fit identifies workouts, not participants, and releases no workout-to-person map, so each workout is treated as its own subject and subject-disjoint splits over this source are only workout-disjoint.
